goal.text: What does a brain-like system perform when implemented computationally, in order to capture neurophysiological (oscillations, spiking) or neuropsychological (attention, distraction) traits observed in empirical studies?
goal.falsifier: Answered-for-now when the graph holds at least one claim node per trait family (oscillatory, spiking, attentional) that names the specific computational operation held responsible AND names a published implementation that reproduces the trait, with the reproduction's measured observable stated. A trait family whose claim rests only on a model that was fit to the trait rather than predicting it does NOT count — that is curve-fitting and must be marked contested.
goal.successor_clause: On closure this respawns as the harder version: which of the named operations are NECESSARY rather than merely sufficient — i.e. which ablations break the trait. That becomes question-implementation-05.
goal.adaptivity: Trait families are not fixed at three. If the corpus grows a fourth with its own evidence cluster (travelling waves, for instance, already has Alamia 2020 and an alpha-travelling-waves entry), Review may split it out, and the falsifier text updates with it.
